title: Live native-step simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $\mathrm{upd}$ update a tag from an optional output bit, and let a two-tape Boolean machine $\mathrm{seek}$ satisfy the following bound $C$: for every Boolean word $w$ encoding an integer $p$ with $p\le |x|+1$, whenever its first tape stores $w$ relative to its head, its second tape is blank, and its state is the designated start state, it reaches the designated finish state in at most $C(|w|+a+p+1)$ steps, where $a$ is its input-head position; before finishing it avoids that state, all work-head displacements are at most $C(|w|+1)$, and at finishing its input-head position is $p$ while its tapes, work-head positions, and output are unchanged. Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $c$ a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and $d$ a four-tape configuration over the recording alphabet on the input obtained by embedding each bit of $x$. Let $D$ be record data whose stored state is present, whose width flag equals the assertion that the binary width of $|x|+1$ is one, and suppose the third work tape of $d$ is blank everywhere. Then there are a bit $b$ and a time $t\le 20(C+1)(\mathrm{width}(|x|)+|x|+1)$ such that the record-step machine, started from the snapshot of $d$ with the read-exit state and with both buffer tapes containing the fixed-width binary digits of $c$'s input-head position, reaches the snapshot with the state and data prescribed by applying $M$'s transition to $D$ with native-right flag $b$ and input symbol read from $c$, with the input-position buffer retained and the second buffer empty. At every earlier time it avoids both verdict states, and throughout the run every work-head displacement from its initial position is at most $(C+1)(\mathrm{width}(|x|)+1)$.
